findings.title: Most secondary text is 11 px
findings.detail: Category labels, milestone counts, unlock lines, money per hour, the day, chips and asset subtitles are 11 px; at 1440x900 they are hard to read at a glance.
findings.fix: Floor of 12 px for secondary text, 13 px for body; data numerals in a wider tabular face.
findings.evidence: contrast.md: fresh@desktop 18 size fails, all 11 px ('Roads', '0 / 10', '+$0/h', 'Day 1', unlock lines)

findings.title: Undo/Redo disabled labels at 1.8:1
findings.detail: Disabled Undo and Redo fade to 40% opacity so their labels are 1.79:1; players can't read what the buttons are until they become active.
findings.fix: Disabled state at ~3:1 (dimmed colour, not opacity), keep label legible.

findings.title: Town label halo is soft; name and size line break up over roads and icons
findings.detail: The town name's text-stroke halo is light cream; over the dark asphalt crossroads and the need icons beneath it, 'VILLAGE · 450' runs into the icons and road markings.
findings.fix: Put the town name on a small enamel nameplate (solid dark ground, cream caps) so contrast is fixed regardless of terrain.

findings.title: The UI has no identity: generic white cards and a pale bar read as a web app, not an industry game
findings.detail: Every surface is the same near-white card with a 1px grey line and soft shadow. Nothing ties the HUD to the company/industrial theme; the owner wants a 1920s-40s Deco industry skin over TF2's dense layout.
findings.fix: Dark enamel-plate panels (navy), cream data text, ochre accent, condensed Deco display face for headings, tabular sans for data.
findings.evidence: --card rgba(255,255,255,.95), --paper #f7f6f1, Lexend everywhere at 11-13 px, blue #1677b3 accent

findings.title: Money and date, the numbers a company player acts on, are small and plain
findings.detail: Money is 13 px bold in the left bar block next to population; the date is 'Day 7' at 11 px. In TF2 the money and date are the anchors of the bottom bar.
findings.fix: Money and clock as stamped numeric readouts (larger tabular digits) in their own plates.

findings.title: Locked cards: name and unlock line wash out
findings.detail: Locked catalog cards dim the icon and name to 45% opacity; 'Iron Mine', 'Coal Mine' etc. read at about 2.3:1 so players can't plan what comes next.
findings.fix: Keep locked names at full legibility in a muted colour, mark lock with a stamped tag.
findings.evidence: industry-catalog@desktop contrast fails on locked card names

findings.title: The tip pulse on Industry looks exactly like the selected Roads button
findings.detail: While Roads is the active category, Industry also shows the selected frame because the hint highlight reuses the same blue border; two categories look active at once.
findings.fix: Give the hint its own treatment (ochre corner tick / underline pulse), distinct from the selected state.
findings.evidence: Roads and Industry both framed blue at x 497-630

findings.title: Panel headings and body text are nearly the same size and weight
findings.detail: The site name (13 px/600), section heads (12 px/600) and body (12 px) differ by a pixel, so a player scanning the Farm panel can't find 'Ready to ship' vs 'Last hour' quickly.
findings.fix: Plate-style title bar (16 px condensed caps) and small-caps section rules distinct from rows.

findings.title: Title card: the game's name is a plain bold web heading
findings.detail: The title menu is the first impression; the name is a 30px Lexend heading on a white card, no sense of era or company.
findings.fix: Enamel nameplate head with a Deco display face and pinstripe rule.

findings.title: Small targets in the junction editor
findings.detail: Arm toggles and duration buttons are 20-22 px tall.

findings.title: Toasts sit behind the milestone banner
findings.detail: A toast fired with a milestone shows at top 56 px, the same place as the banner, so it is hidden.
findings.fix: Move toasts below the banner zone or above the bottom bar.
findings.evidence: toasts 'Game saved', 'Not enough money' not visible in milestone shot
